title: Choose a reading typeface, do not inherit one
intent: Make the body type a decision with a reason rather than the first font in a starter template.
when_to_use: any page whose primary content is text
the page must carry a point of view without spending colour or imagery
when_not_to_use: the artifact is a throwaway internal note where the typeface has no audience
the surface is a dense tool where the platform UI font genuinely reads better and is the fastest thing to render
rules: the body font stack is declared and its first entry is neither Inter nor a bare system stack without a stated reason
the first entry of the stack is a family that ships with the artifact or is loaded explicitly; no stack starts with an undefined name
body size is at least 16px and line height sits between 1.4 and 1.7 times the body size
the type scale has at least four steps and no two adjacent steps differ by less than 1.15 times
trade_off: A chosen typeface adds a loading decision, a licence question, and a fallback metric problem, while the system stack is free and always available.
failure_mode: A fashionable face is loaded for headings and reused for body copy at small size, or the stack asks for a weight the page never ships, so the browser synthesises it and the text looks damaged.

example.brief: Long form research summary read on desktop and phone.
example.ruling: A serif with real text sizes for body at 17px and 1.6 line height, a neutral sans for interface text only, four scale steps with a 1.25 ratio, and both families shipped rather than requested.
